transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Product); Lena Morales (AuroraCloud PM), Amit Shah (Aurora Solutions Architect), Priya Rao (Aurora Marketplace Ops), Carlos Jimenez (Aurora Security)

Summary:
Quick technical sync between Redwood and AuroraCloud to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for joint solution (hosted + private options), and next steps for a joint PRD. Discussed security artifacts (SOC2/KMS/SAML), technical integration points (VPC peering, private control plane, billing metadata), and PoC plan for perf/latency validation.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing metadata & screenshots
- Reference architecture for Redwood Private + Aurora managed marketplace integration
- VPC peering, private control plane, and KMS/HSM considerations
- Deployment variants (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and recommended templates
- Billing & SKU mapping for marketplace listing
- Security/compliance handoff and evidence (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary)
- PoC test plan and owner alignment

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for doing this, appreciate it. We're running about an hour, maybe an hour ten, try to cover listing metadata then Sofia will dive into the VPC and private deployment bits.
[00:12] Lena: Thanks Jordan, we put together a rough agenda, want to make sure we get the reference arch aligned so it matches our marketplace reqs.
[00:18] Amit: Yeah and from infra side we want to understand peering requirements and what logs/Audit we'll need.
[00:24] Sofia: Great. Quick intro on the Redwood side - Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options; for marketplace we typically list the hosted offering and a reference arch that covers private deployment.
[00:37] Priya: For marketplace ops we need a SKU, pricing bands, screenshots, a 1-line, 30-word, and 150-word description plus a reference arch diagram. Do you have an example?
[00:47] Jordan: Yep we'll share our canonical listing template. I'll attach a spreadsheet that maps our fields to Aurora's marketplace fields. Expect screenshots and a short demo vid example.
[00:56] Marcus: On the product side, maybe call out the smart routing/fallback behavior in the 150-word description - customers care about availability across regions.
[01:05] Lena: Good call. Also need to know if private deployments show up as separate SKUs or as an add-on.
[01:12] Jordan: Typically marketplace shows hosted as primary SKU and private as a managed deployment add-on. But open to mapping how Aurora prefers.
[01:19] Amit: Technical - for VPC peering what IP ranges and ports do you need? What's your control plane traffic like?
[01:27] Sofia: For Private we have a control plane that can be either customer-managed or Redwood-managed in a private VPC. Peering requires outbound TLS on 443 to our control endpoints, and then a set of internal ports for the data plane depending on whether GPU nodes are in customer VPC. We'll send a detailed network appendix.
[01:45] Carlos: On security, we need SOC2 type II, encryption at rest KMS integration, and SSO - SAML or OIDC. Also, audit logs and maybe HSM support for keys.
[01:55] Jordan: We have SOC2 on file, can share the attestation. KMS integrations are supported - we have a KMS abstraction layer and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. SSO via SAML is supported, we'll note that in the docs.
[02:04] Priya: Marketplace requires a security blurb and a link to attestation. Can we provide a short whitepaper?
[02:10] Marcus: We'll prepare a short security summary and link to the SOC2 report redacted version and a compliance pack.
[02:18] Amit: Performance - we want to test p95 latency for the Aurora region, and also a throughput run to validate burst capacity for our enterprise customers. How do you recommend we run a PoC?
[02:29] Sofia: Proposed PoC: 1) baseline perf on hosted in Aurora region across 3 payload sizes, 2) Private deployment in a test VPC with a small Dedicated pool to validate KV cache and batching behavior, 3) run integration tests for auth and logging. We'll provide a test plan with targets.
[02:45] Lena: Timeline? We want listing live by mid-June ideally.
[02:49] Jordan: That seems doable if we get docs and security artifacts in early May and run PoC in mid-May.
[02:56] Carlos: A note on data residency - customers in EU need logs retained in-region; does Redwood support regionally isolated deployments?
[03:03] Sofia: Yes, regional isolation is supported via Dedicated pools pinned to regions or Private with customer-managed infra - we'll include region options in the reference arch.
[03:12] Amit: For peering, our infra team will need an exact CIDR and BGP info if you're doing cross-VPC routing.
[03:18] Jordan: We'll ask Sofia to provide the network appendix.
[03:22] (crosstalk)
[03:26] Sofia: One thing to flag, if Aurora wants marketplace billing to flow through Aurora we need to map SKUs to your metering fields and provide a lightweight usage export or billing hook. We support usage-based metering and can export metered tokens / embedding units per day.
[03:41] Priya: How granular is that metering? Marketplace expects daily usage by SKU plus some labels for org/customer.
[03:48] Marcus: We can emit daily aggregates and per-tenant breakdowns in a CSV or push to an API endpoint. There may be PII concerns but it's mostly numeric usage counts.
[03:58] Carlos: Any pen test or third-party attestation we can share?
[04:02] Jordan: We did a pen test last quarter - redacted report is available. We'll add it to the compliance pack.
[04:08] Lena: On the reference arch, we need a diag that shows SSO flow, KMS, peering, and optional dedicated GPU pool. Can you do both a simple and an advanced variant?
[04:17] Marcus: Yes, we'll produce a simple 'hosted + listing' diagram and an advanced 'private + managed control plane + HSM' variant.
[04:26] Amit: On the integration side, do you have a terraform module or IaC for private deployments?
[04:30] Sofia: We provide a reference Terraform module and some example CloudFormation snippets. They aren't productized as a provider, but they are used in our Private runbooks. We'll share repo links.
[04:40] Priya: Content assets - we need screenshots of the console, sample API requests, and a partner logo.
[04:45] Jordan: We'll export console screenshots and a short 60s demo snippet. Also will include sample curl/python snippets for the marketplace listing blurb.
[04:53] (background noise)
[05:01] Carlos: On keys - HSM support, do you offer customer-managed keys for encrypting model weights or just for metadata?
[05:07] Sofia: Currently KMS/HSM integration is for data at rest (customer data, logs). For model artifacts we support encryption at rest; if a customer requires HSM-wrapped keys for weights that's an advanced enterprise option we can discuss with eng.
[05:20] Amit: Ok, good to note. For the PoC we'll probably start with test keys and move to KMS later.
[05:26] Lena: Marketplace approval process - what's the typical review time from Redwood side once we submit?
[05:33] Jordan: Once we receive your marketplace mapping and security checklist, Redwood will review our internal docs and any required engineering support. We aim for 7-10 business days for our side to prepare artifacts, not counting any infra PoC time.
[05:45] Priya: For support level, do you offer a joint support routing for customers who buy via Aurora?
[05:51] Marcus: We can set up a joint support pathway and an integration guide that references Aurora's support. For enterprise deals we also offer an SSO-linked support escalation.
[05:59] Carlos: Quick question - do you record audit logs to a customer-managed location or do we pull them from your endpoint?
[06:05] Sofia: We can stream audit logs to a customer-managed S3 or push to an endpoint. We'll include log formats in the appendix.
[06:12] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps -
[06:15] Jordan: Action items - I'll send the marketplace field mapping and screenshots by May 4. Sofia will share the network appendix and PoC plan by May 6. Carlos will send security questionnaire by May 7. Lena and Marcus to collaborate on the one-pager by May 14. Priya to confirm required assets by May 3.
[06:33] Lena: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:36] Amit: We'll follow up with infra contacts and set a peering window.
[06:40] Jordan: Great. We'll re-schedule a runbook review the week of May 11 - I'll send a calendar invite.
[06:46] (end)

Notes / Links shared during call:
